Bread begins with only four ingredients: flour, water, salt and yeast. The baker mixes them into a rough dough and lets it rest, so the flour can absorb the water. Then the dough is folded and stretched until it becomes smooth and elastic. During a slow rise, the yeast fills it with tiny bubbles of gas. Finally the loaf goes into a hot oven, where the crust turns golden and the kitchen fills with a warm, familiar smell that brings the whole family to the table.
